entry.title: Polygonal latrine remains, Villa Romana del Casale

groundCutout.basis: Nine occupied masonry strips only; open center and west entrance retain native terrain.

buildingCutout.basis: Shared park Q505617 identifies the site; independent way412339872/native35184784428704 identifies this separate southern polygonal latrine. Its eight mapped vertices set meter scale and offsets. Internal +X points east-southeast away from the villa and +Z follows the western side south-southwest. Native east/up/south axes are baked with heading 0. Only this one footprint is replaced; the northern eastern latrine and every other building remain independent.

terrainReference.basis: Qualified approximate native exterior fit on original Protomaps20261020/Mapzen 201x201 / 6m ground. Open eastern provider [4,0] supplies 554.4101060817029m datum. Boundary grades -0.941..+0.026m; each of nine closed masonry bases extends 0.15m below its own footprint minimum. Current native views show supported low walls with modest grade-related exposure/burial, a clear west gap and original open center/approaches. Only masonry strips mask terrain; all 42 resident / 43 wider independent buildings, original grid/roads and empty water layer remain. Exact archaeological floor/paving, thresholds, wall preservation and accessibility are unverified. No bespoke terrain or flattening.
